title: Generators can emit arcs with a chord under 1 um

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Refs #3442

## Problem

The 2D generators can emit an arc whose chord is shorter than 1 micrometre. No arc path in the CL or in the motion crate has a minimum chord or a minimum sweep. After #3442, each shipped post writes such an arc as a straight move or as no block, so the posted program is safe. But the toolpath, the simulation and the CL file still carry an arc that no output format can show.

## Sites (found by a read, not by a run)

- `crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs` `push_arc` and `push_arc_in`: the only test is that the end differs from the start. There is no chord floor.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/fillet.rs`: the sweep is at least 0.5 degrees and the radius floor is `MIN_BLEND_RADIUS = 0.01` mm. The chord can therefore be about 0.09 um.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arcs.rs` `fit_arcs_sided`: the split pieces are index-based. A piece over clustered input vertices can possibly have a sub-micrometre chord. This is not tested.
- `crates/motion/src/entry_arc.rs` `arc_lead_swept`: the sweep has no floor in this code. Where the `arc_sweep` parameter is validated was not read.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_biarc.rs`: no chord floor.

The rings already have a floor: `MIN_ARC_CHORD = 0.01` mm in `crates/motion/src/ring_zig.rs`, used by `ring_walk` and `push_zig_ring`.

## Done means

- Each arc-emitting generator emits a straight segment (or nothing) in place of an arc whose chord is under one law, for example `MIN_ARC_CHORD`.
- A test pins each site with a fixture that would emit a sub-micrometre arc today.
- The CL input law does not change: a short arc in an outside `.cnc` file stays legal input (#3442).
